title: The Three Accommodations by Which the Lord's Operative Power Orders the Natural
reading:
When the Lord comes to act upon the natural mind as operative power, he does not enter it bare. He clothes himself in three accommodations — in thought, in love, and in truth at the natural degree — and works through these as through garments fitted to the rational. Wearing them, he reaches into the substrate the proprium has been forming and lays his hand on every work that has been thrown up there. What had exalted itself above and what had sunk below he brings together under one ordering and subordinates them; the disordered productions of self-love are set, by his operation in these three vehicles, beneath their proper measure.

Then, the work being done, the garments are stripped from him. The accommodations were never the Lord himself; they were the form he took to operate at that degree, and once they have served he lays them off from the midst of what has been ordered, leaving the rational standing upright in what is righteous within it.

Then comes the scattering. What had been claimed and gathered into the proprium's mass is broken up and dispersed — not destroyed, but loosened from its claim — so that what is the Lord's within it may be purified and what is not may fall away. He fixes what is purified within those three accommodated registers, holding it firm at the lower bound, at the limits of the natural's whole circuit, still wearing the form by which he reaches that depth.

And then the upward motion: what has been purified is raised, conveyed up through the degrees toward the upper place, returning to that height from which the operative power had first been sent forth. This is the whole circuit — the Lord coming down clothed, ordering the natural through accommodated form, stripping the form when its work is done, scattering what was claimed for purification, and bearing what is purified upward into conjunction with the source from which the descent began.
